title: ChatGPT and Codex Share One Usage Pool Starting December
summary: OpenAI unifies ChatGPT and Codex token allowances in December 2026 for Plus, Pro, and Business plans. One shared pool changes how subscribers budget usage.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- OpenAI will merge ChatGPT and Codex into one shared token allowance for Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers starting December 2026.
- Heavy Codex coding sessions will now consume the same credit balance as ChatGPT chat work, requiring users to budget usage differently.
- Pro plans retain their no-5-hour-limit advantage, but all paid tiers will draw from a unified token pool measured in credits per million tokens.


OpenAI confirmed on October 31, 2026, that ChatGPT and Codex will share a single token allowance starting in December 2026. The change applies to all Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers and replaces the separate per-product usage pools currently in place. Under the new structure, every coding session in Codex and every conversation in ChatGPT will draw from the same unified credit balance, measured in tokens across all models.


## What Changes in December


The unified allowance consolidates two previously separate buckets into one shared pool. Tokens are the small chunks of text that AI models read and write, and OpenAI has used them as the basis for usage pricing since April 2026. Before that shift, OpenAI counted usage by message, treating a short question and a compute-intensive request as roughly equivalent units. The token-based approach better reflects the computational demands of different tasks, particularly for advanced models.


Starting in December, a heavy afternoon of Codex work will eat into the same allowance a subscriber would otherwise spend on ChatGPT email rewrites or brainstorming sessions. For developers who split time between coding and chatting, this introduces a new kind of internal competition within a single account. Teams that lean heavily on Codex may find their general ChatGPT usage squeezed as a result.


## Which Plans Are Affected


The change covers OpenAI's three main paid tiers: Plus, Pro, and Business. Plan structures still differ in important ways. Pro plans do not carry a 5-hour usage limit, while Plus and Business plans do. Pro users may still face weekly caps, though OpenAI has not clarified exactly how those caps will interact with the combined allowance. Plus and Business customers should monitor whether the 5-hour limits become more restrictive once Codex draws from the same balance.


Pro plan allowances have seen notable adjustments in 2026. In October, OpenAI doubled the allowances for Pro 100 and Pro 500 tiers. A planned reduction for Pro 200 was canceled. Codex users also received temporary doublings of usage limits in late December 2025. These frequent adjustments suggest that current numbers could move again as OpenAI refines its pricing model.


## Release Date and Implementation


Officially launched on December 2026, the unified allowance system will take effect at the start of the month. OpenAI announced the change through a help-center update that gained traction on Hacker News, accumulating 164 points, and sparked multiple threads on Reddit's r/OpenAI forum under the label "allowance enforcement." The policy shift follows OpenAI's broader[token-based pricing](https://emergent.sh/glossary/usage-based-pricing) overhaul that began in April 2026.


## Implications for Subscribers


For Business customers, a single metered balance is easier to track and forecast than two separate pools. Finance teams can now monitor one unified usage number instead of splitting attention between chat and coding budgets. Developers gain flexibility: unused ChatGPT credits no longer sit idle when Codex capacity runs out. However, teams that rely heavily on one product over the other may need to rethink their workflows.


Several open questions remain. How weekly caps on Pro plans will interact with the combined allowance is unclear. Whether Plus and Business users will find the 5-hour limits more restrictive once Codex draws from the same balance is another unknown. OpenAI's history of pricing adjustments, including doublings and canceled reductions, suggests that subscribers should not assume current limits are permanent.


## What This Means


The unified allowance removes friction for users who work across both ChatGPT and Codex but introduces new tradeoffs. Anyone building workflows around current limits should expect that the numbers could shift again. Starting in December 2026, every prompt and every line of generated code will draw from the same well. Subscribers who split time between chatting and coding should start paying attention to which activities consume the most tokens, because the balance you manage is now the only balance you have.
